about: What an agent's answer is held to (`answers-with:`, `checked-by:`, `checks-at-most:`). Replayed as conformance_kit.replay_agent does: `model` is the lead agent's turns, turn N being what the model writes when the conversation it is sent holds N replies of its own, so a reply that was not the answer and was asked for again is followed by the next turn; `tools` is what each tool hands back. The rules these hold: a reply that would be the answer is held to the shape the agent says it gives (a field left out does not fit unless its line says `, optional`; a value its line refuses does not fit; a field the agent does not declare is not a reason to ask again and is not handed back) and, when it fits, to the agent's own `checked-by:` rules. One that is not the answer is asked for again, the model told why at its next request and at no other, last in its system text (`asked-again`). It is asked for at most `checks-at-most:` times in all, 2 when unwritten, the shape and the rules spending from one count; an empty reply that arrived is one of them. Still not the answer, the run ends `checks-failed`, its `output` says how many times it was asked and what was wrong with the last reply, and it hands back no `answer`. An agent that declares no shape and no rules is held to nothing. The closing answer of a run that reached a limit (`when-it-runs-out: answer-with-what-it-has`) is held the same way, from the same count: asked again, the closing request is the same request and then why; never fitting, the run keeps its ceiling's own word in `halted`, because it did run out, and its `output` says it was left with no answer. In `expect`: `said` is what the model wrote at each step, a reply that was not the answer included; `answer` is each declared field the answer carried, as written; `output` is the reply as the model wrote it, or what the run says when it has no answer.
